sources: Radio Taiwan International (RTI) Oct 30 18:16 +08; Arab Times Online carrying Bloomberg Oct 28-29
fault_line: Self-defeating subservience to Beijing vs loyal strategic alignment: does the ban cost Pakistan more than it buys?

sections.what_happened: [FOLLOW-UP to 1400-06] NEW IN-WINDOW: Taiwan's Premier Cho Jung-Tai said Friday Oct 30 the government will safeguard Taiwan's sovereignty and international aviation rights; Foreign Minister Lin Chia-lung said Friday morning Pakistan's actions were 'self-defeating and in violation of international aviation rules' and urged ICAO to take the incident seriously; Transport Minister Chen Shih-kai called it a civil aviation matter and hoped political factors would not interfere. MISSED CATCH-UP (strengthens 1400-06): Pakistan Defence Minister Khawaja Asif confirmed to Bloomberg that Pakistan barred Taiwanese airlines under its One-China policy: 'The aviation division follows the One China policy -- only mainland China is allowed.' Flight-tracking showed China Airlines and EVA Air stopped overflying Pakistan from the morning of Oct 25, rerouting south over the Gulf or north over Russia. Taipei's suspicion that 'definitely China was behind this' (Chen Ming-chi, AFP) remains an allegation, not proof; Asif's statement establishes Pakistan's own stated basis, not Beijing's role.
sections.what_verified: Taipei officials' Friday statements via RTI; closure + rerouting via AFP (Manila Times/Khaleej Times Oct 29-30); Asif confirmation via Bloomberg as carried by Arab Times. Taipei's 'China behind it' attribution is NOT corroborated by Asif's statement.
sections.what_disputed: Neither airline would confirm to AFP that Pakistan had closed or reopened its airspace; Pakistan says the ban was lifted only temporarily 'till the end of the winter'; critics note China itself allows Taiwanese airlines in its airspace, undercutting the solidarity logic (social debate).
sections.why_matters: First country ever to bar Taiwanese airlines on One-China grounds -- and Taipei just answered: 'self-defeating'. Pakistan confirmed it itself.
sections.context: Background: FOLLOW-UP to 1400-06 (in-window Taipei reaction + Islamabad confirmation) -- Taiwan's Friday official response to Pakistan's airspace closure; Pakistan's defence minister confirms the One-China-policy basis to Bloomberg

totw_analysis: Our read: First country ever to bar Taiwanese airlines on One-China grounds -- and Taipei just answered: 'self-defeating'. Pakistan confirmed it itself. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Self-defeating subservience to Beijing vs loyal strategic alignment: does the ban cost Pakistan more than it buys?
